verdict.rationale: Wally Cloud documents a hosted tier that runs models on RunAnywhere's hardware, so users can use models too large for a laptop with the same tools. Users select it explicitly with a `--cloud` flag or through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and Wally never silently routes requests between local and hosted. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that cloud use needs no local model download, a documented list of which large models are offered, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the cloud tier.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can offload very large models to a hosted cloud tier without downloading them when my local hardware is insufficient

citations.quote: Cloud models run on RunAnywhere's hardware instead of the user's, so you can use models too large for a laptop while keeping the same tools.
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
Hosted and local execution are explicit choices. Wally does not silently move a request between them.
The endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so the official OpenAI clients work by pointing `base_url` at it.
